1	/**
2	 * Article body chunker with overlap.
3	 *
4	 * Splits long text into overlapping chunks suitable for independent embedding.
5	 * Chunk-based retrieval beats whole-document embedding in practice:
6	 *   - A 4000-char article has one averaged representation; important details wash out.
7	 *   - A 4000-char article split into 8 × 600-char chunks surfaces specific passages.
8	 *
9	 * We use character-based sizing (not token-based) because:
10	 *   - No tokenizer dependency at ingestion time.
11	 *   - Gemini's embedding model accepts up to ~2048 tokens; 2000 chars is well within that.
12	 *   - Character boundaries preserve natural paragraph/sentence breaks when possible.
13	 *
14	 * Chunking algorithm:
15	 *   1. If the text is short (≤ `maxChunkSize`), return a single chunk.
16	 *   2. Otherwise, walk forward in steps of `maxChunkSize - overlap`.
17	 *   3. At each step, cut at the nearest sentence/paragraph boundary within a
18	 *      small window, so chunks end at semantically meaningful points.
19	 */

1	# ADR-0004: One opaque article ref; deterministic chunk refs
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).
6	
7	## Decision
8	
9	An article has exactly one public identity: `art-<yyyymmdd>-<hex8>` (acquisition date plus 8 random hex characters, the repo's run-id style), minted once by Feed at first acquisition and carrying no publisher, title, or URL semantics. Chunk refs derive from it deterministically: `<article_ref>#r<revision>:<start>-<end>` for span chunks (half-open character offsets in UTF-16 code units into that revision's stored body) and `<article_ref>#p:<post_id>` for live-update chunks. Identity lives in the ref; everything informative (title, publisher, URL, dates, hashes) lives in response fields. Only Feed mints refs: consumers deriving their own identities for feed content (as the pipeline adapter did with a projection hash) is banned. `url_hash`, `content_hash`, and `title_hash` remain internal dedup attributes and never cross the boundary.
10	
11	## Considered options
12	
13	- Promote the legible file ids (`art-<date>-<site>-<slug>`) to public refs: rejected. Embedded site/date/title invite parsing (Hyrum's law) and become lies after alias flips (ADR-0006) or upstream corrections; the current minting also has a live collision defect (the filename gets a dedup counter, the id does not; 13 shared-id pairs exist across the 21,138 article rows as of 2026-07-10).
14	- Typed-prefix ULIDs: rejected. Monotonicity at scale is a property we do not need, and it breaks the repo's legible date+hex token style.
15	
16	## Consequences
17	
18	- Deterministic chunk-ref derivation is what lets the chunk layer stay a rebuildable index (ADR-0008) without breaking refs anyone holds.
19	- The span unit (UTF-16 code units) is part of the public contract and needs a non-ASCII fixture test.
20	- Backfill mints refs for every existing article; old file ids remain as file names only.
